headline: ISS RECOMMENDS FOR ON BOTH SIDES — $18.5B EQUINOX/ORLA NORTH AMERICA NO. 2 GOLD MINER DEAL CLEARS FINAL HURDLE
snippet: Independent proxy advisory firms including Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) issued separate voting recommendations on July 10 for shareholders of both Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) and Orla Mining (NYSE: ORLA) to vote FOR the all-share business combination, with ISS noting the deal 'appears to make strategic sense' by diversifying Equinox's asset base and improving long-term production potential — clearing the last major advisory hurdle before the July 22 special shareholder meetings, with proxy voting deadline July 20. Unanimous board support on both sides plus ISS backing creates the clearest possible institutional validation for the deal that creates a 1.1 million oz/yr North American gold producer at an $18.5 billion combined market value.

headline: HONG KONG LAUNCHES RIVAL GOLD CLEARING SYSTEM — 41 BANKS, 'HAU' BENCHMARK, SHANGHAI DIRECT LINK CHALLENGE LBMA MONOPOLY
snippet: Hong Kong launched the trial operation of its Gold Central Clearing and Settlement System on July 7, 2026, completing its first batch of transactions with 41 participating institutions and introducing the 'HAU' price code as Asia's new gold pricing benchmark — simultaneously activating the first phase of physical connectivity with the Shanghai Gold Exchange to create a direct settlement pipeline outside the LBMA Gold Price fix. For mining investors the structural consequence is price discovery: if Asia captures meaningful gold pricing influence during its trading hours, gold benchmarks will increasingly reflect physical demand from the world's two largest sovereign buyers, a structural tailwind for producers whose NAV is leveraged to the gold price rather than Western speculative flows.

headline: HSBC CUTS 2026 GOLD FORECAST TO $4,560 AVERAGE — HAWKISH FED TILT SETS $3,800 FLOOR, $4,750 YEAR-END
snippet: HSBC cut its 2026 average gold price forecast to $4,560/oz (from $4,864) and 2027 to $4,925 (from $5,000) on July 9, citing 'changing perceptions of U.S. monetary policy and the impact this had on the dollar,' projecting a $3,800–$4,700 trading range for the rest of 2026 and a $4,750 year-end target. HSBC's downgrade is the institutional bear case sitting opposite Goldman Sachs ($4,900 year-end), JP Morgan ($4,800–$6,300), and the World Gold Council's upside scenario: if the July 14 CPI print pushes September hike probability above 65%, the $3,800 floor becomes the reference point rather than the bullish consensus targets.

headline: ALKANE DRILLS DEEPEST BJÖRKDAL HIT YET: GOLD AT 762M — STORHEDEN DEPOSIT EXTENDS OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS (ASX:ALK / TSX:ALK)
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK, TSX: ALK) reported July 8 that extension drilling at the Björkdal Gold Mine in northern Sweden intersected high-grade gold at 762 metres — the project's deepest intersection yet — as part of a 29-hole program targeting the Storheden deposit's Eastern and Northern extensions, confirming the orebody remains open in multiple directions well below existing stope limits. Alkane acquired Björkdal outright through its August 2025 merger with Mandalay Resources; extending the deposit at depth in Sweden's stable permitting environment with Baltic Sea shipping access directly re-rates the mine's remaining life and NAV without additional regulatory risk, at $4,100/oz gold.

headline: FORTUNA Q2 72,217 GEO — SÉGUÉLA 2.3 MTA EXPANSION CONSTRUCTION DECISION IMMINENT, FATAL ACCIDENT NOTED (NYSE:FSM / TSX:FVI)
snippet: Fortuna Mining (TSX: FVI, NYSE: FSM) reported July 9 Q2 2026 production of 72,217 gold equivalent ounces — broadly in line with 71,229 GEO in Q2 2025 — putting H1 2026 at 145,089 GEO and the company on track for its 281,000–305,000 GEO full-year guidance across three mines in Côte d'Ivoire, Mexico, and Burkina Faso; Lycopodium completed a Séguéla expansion study in late June targeting a capacity increase to approximately 2.3 million tonnes per annum, with a construction decision expected 'in the coming weeks.' The report also discloses a fatal accident involving a contractor employee at the Séguéla haul truck circuit, with an investigation completed and learnings incorporated; the expansion decision is the most important near-term catalyst for FSM as a positive outcome at current gold prices creates unmodelled NAV upside from Fortuna's highest-grade, lowest-cost flagship.

headline: CORE SILVER MERGES WITH ARCUS 1-FOR-1 — C$6.5M CASH, TOULEARY VMS ANCHORS YUKON TINTINA BELT PLATFORM (TSXV:CC / ADG)
snippet: Core Silver Corp (TSXV: CC) and Arcus Development Group (TSXV: ADG) announced July 9 a definitive arrangement agreement for Core Silver to acquire all Arcus shares on a 1:1 all-share basis — creating a combined entity with approximately C$6.5 million in cash and a consolidated exploration portfolio anchored by the Touleary VMS discovery in Yukon's Tintina Gold Belt, a drill-confirmed volcanogenic massive sulphide system with permits in place for the 2026 field season and multiple untested targets; Arcus shareholders vote Aug. 25, closing expected Q4 2026. The Tintina's Finlayson segment hosts some of Canada's highest-grade VMS deposits, and two under-capitalised exploration companies merging on the strength of a drill-confirmed VMS discovery is exactly the consolidation pattern that precedes the systematic delineation of district-scale copper-zinc systems — at $6+/lb copper and structurally short Western VMS supply.

headline: CRITICAL METALS RETAINS CLEAR STREET TO FOCUS ON TANBREEZ — GREENLAND'S LARGEST UNDEVELOPED REE DEPOSIT TAKES CENTRE STAGE (NASDAQ:CRML)
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) announced July 8 that it has retained Clear Street as financial advisor to evaluate sale or spin-off structures for non-core legacy assets, with the explicit goal of concentrating capital allocation on the Tanbreez rare earth project in southern Greenland — a 92.5%-owned deposit described as one of the world's largest undeveloped rare earth resources, with year-round deep-water fjord access to the North Atlantic. With all 18 rare earth elements rallying simultaneously in July's 16.7% average surge and Project Vault driving systematic U.S. REE stockpiling, CRML's pivot to Tanbreez-first capital allocation is strategically rational — though the market's modest negative reaction to the July 8 announcement signals that investors need to see the non-core monetization close and development capital flow to Greenland before repricing the Tanbreez option.

headline: GOLCONDA GOLD SUMMIT MINE: FIRST ORE TO SURFACE JULY 7 — WET COMMISSIONING AND FIRST CONCENTRATE TARGETED BY SEPTEMBER (ASX:GCX)
snippet: Golconda Gold (ASX: GCX) reported July 9 that the Galaxy Gold Mine in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa produced 3,648 ounces in Q2 2026 — consistent with Q1 and 20% above Q2 2025 — while announcing that first ore from the Summit Mine in New Mexico was delivered to surface on July 7, 2026, with wet commissioning of the plant and first concentrate production targeted by the end of September. Summit is a high-grade underground gold mine in the Black Range of New Mexico: bringing it to first concentrate within a Canadian-listed, dual-hemisphere producer structure gives Golconda exposure to U.S. domestic gold production at a moment when the Trump administration's critical minerals policy is actively differentiating American-sourced precious metals from offshore supply chains.
